label: Occupancy rate
definition: The share of available bed days that were filled by residents during the cost-reporting period.
formula: Total resident days / total bed days available
strategic_use: Used to assess capacity utilization, demand, referral strength, and whether the facility is carrying excess bed capacity.
high_value_interpretation: Higher occupancy generally suggests stronger demand or better use of available capacity, but very high occupancy can reduce flexibility.
low_value_interpretation: Lower occupancy may suggest referral leakage, market competition, quality/reputation issues, or excess capacity.
trend_interpretation: A declining trend may be a warning sign for market position; an improving trend may suggest stronger referral capture or demand recovery.
caveats: Occupancy alone does not prove financial strength. Interpret it with payer mix, margin, staffing, and quality.

label: Medicare day share
definition: The share of total resident days paid by Medicare.
strategic_use: Used as a proxy for skilled/post-acute orientation and hospital referral capture.
high_value_interpretation: A higher share may reflect stronger post-acute volume, more skilled care, or greater Medicare payment exposure.
low_value_interpretation: A lower share may indicate a more long-stay/custodial model or weaker skilled referral capture.
trend_interpretation: A declining trend may indicate loss of post-acute referrals or a shift toward long-stay utilization.
caveats: This is not a direct case-mix measure and should eventually be interpreted with quality, PBJ staffing, hospital referral data, and Medicare Advantage context.

label: Medicaid day share
definition: The share of total resident days paid by Medicaid.
strategic_use: Used to assess long-stay payer dependence and exposure to state Medicaid reimbursement policy.
high_value_interpretation: A higher share often reflects a long-stay nursing facility business model and may increase reimbursement adequacy risk.
low_value_interpretation: A lower share may reflect a more post-acute, private-pay, or other-payer business mix.
trend_interpretation: A rising trend may indicate increasing dependence on long-stay Medicaid volume.
caveats: High Medicaid share is not automatically negative; it must be interpreted with state Medicaid rates, occupancy, costs, and margin.

label: Other/private day share
definition: The share of resident days not classified as Medicare or Medicaid in the cost report.
strategic_use: Used as a broad proxy for private pay, managed care, commercial, or other payer activity.
high_value_interpretation: A higher share may reflect payer diversity or private/managed-care activity.
low_value_interpretation: A lower share may indicate heavier reliance on Medicare and Medicaid programs.
trend_interpretation: A changing trend may suggest shifts in payer contracts, resident mix, or local market dynamics.
caveats: The category is broad and should not be treated as a clean private-pay measure without additional payer detail.

label: Net patient revenue per resident day
definition: Net patient care revenue divided by total resident days.
formula: Net patient revenue / total resident days
strategic_use: Used to evaluate revenue yield, reimbursement adequacy, payer mix, and payment performance.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value may reflect stronger skilled mix, better reimbursement, higher acuity, or more favorable payer contracts.
low_value_interpretation: A lower value may reflect Medicaid dependence, weaker payer contracts, lower acuity, or limited skilled volume.
trend_interpretation: Revenue/day should be compared with expense/day to identify margin compression or improvement.
caveats: Revenue per day should not be interpreted without payer mix and case-mix context.

label: Operating expense per resident day
definition: Total operating expense divided by total resident days.
strategic_use: Used to assess cost intensity, operating efficiency, labor pressure, and sustainability.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value may reflect higher staffing costs, contract labor, acuity, overhead, or inefficiency.
low_value_interpretation: A lower value may reflect efficiency, lower labor costs, lower acuity, or possible underinvestment.
trend_interpretation: If expenses grow faster than revenue/day, margin pressure may increase.
caveats: Lower expense is not always better. Interpret with staffing, quality, acuity, and occupancy.

label: Patient service margin
definition: Net income from patient care services as a share of net patient revenue.
formula: Net income from service to patients / net patient revenue
strategic_use: Used to assess whether patient care operations are financially sustainable.
high_value_interpretation: A positive margin suggests care delivery revenue is covering related operating costs.
low_value_interpretation: A negative margin suggests patient care operations are not covering costs.
trend_interpretation: A worsening trend may indicate revenue pressure, cost growth, payer-mix deterioration, or staffing pressure.
caveats: This metric does not explain why margin is high or low; use it with revenue/day, expense/day, payer mix, and labor metrics.

label: Total margin
definition: Overall net income as a share of net patient revenue.
strategic_use: Used to evaluate total financial performance after considering non-patient revenue or other income effects.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value indicates stronger overall surplus relative to care revenue.
low_value_interpretation: A lower or negative value indicates weaker overall financial performance.
trend_interpretation: A trend can reveal whether total profitability is improving or deteriorating.
caveats: Total margin can be influenced by accounting, ownership structure, related-party activity, and other income.

label: Salary cost per resident day
definition: Adjusted salary expense divided by total resident days.
strategic_use: Used to assess direct labor cost intensity and compare staffing-cost pressure across peers.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value may indicate higher staffing levels, higher wages, acuity, or labor-market pressure.
low_value_interpretation: A lower value may reflect efficiency, lower wage markets, lower staffing intensity, or possible underinvestment.
trend_interpretation: A rising trend may indicate wage inflation, staffing changes, or acuity changes.
caveats: Cost-report salary data does not directly measure staffing hours or quality; PBJ staffing should be added for stronger interpretation.

label: Contract labor per resident day
definition: Contract labor expense divided by total resident days.
strategic_use: Used to assess agency or contracted labor cost pressure on a per-resident-day basis.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value may signal staffing shortages, agency reliance, or temporary labor-market disruption.
low_value_interpretation: A lower value may indicate limited contract-labor reliance or stronger employee staffing stability.
trend_interpretation: A rising trend may be an early indicator of staffing stress or wage pressure.
caveats: Some contract labor can be normal or temporary; pair with PBJ staffing and local labor-market context.

label: Contract labor ratio
definition: Contract labor as a share of combined adjusted salaries and contract labor.
strategic_use: Used to assess workforce instability and reliance on contracted or agency staffing.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value may indicate staffing shortages, retention problems, agency dependence, or labor-market stress.
low_value_interpretation: A lower value may indicate more stable employed staffing or less dependence on agency labor.
trend_interpretation: A rising trend is often a warning sign for operating cost and staffing stability.
caveats: This is a financial proxy, not a staffing-hours measure; PBJ data should be added for stronger operations analysis.

label: Days cash on hand
definition: Estimated number of days the facility could cover operating expenses using reported cash.
strategic_use: Used to assess liquidity cushion and short-term financial resilience.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value suggests more liquidity cushion.
low_value_interpretation: A lower value may indicate financial fragility or limited cash reserves.
trend_interpretation: A declining trend can signal weakening liquidity even before margins become severely negative.
caveats: Balance sheet values can be affected by timing, ownership structure, related parties, and accounting practices.

label: Current ratio
definition: Current assets divided by current liabilities.
strategic_use: Used to evaluate short-term ability to cover obligations due within a year.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value generally suggests stronger short-term liquidity.
low_value_interpretation: A lower value may signal near-term financial pressure or limited working capital.
trend_interpretation: A declining trend can indicate growing liquidity risk.
caveats: Interpret with days cash, payables, accounts receivable, and ownership context.

label: Days accounts receivable
definition: Estimated days of net patient revenue tied up in accounts receivable.
formula: Accounts receivable / (net patient revenue / report days)
strategic_use: Used to assess billing, collection timing, and working-capital pressure.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value may indicate slower collections, payer delays, or billing issues.
low_value_interpretation: A lower value may suggest faster collections or a less receivables-intensive payer mix.
trend_interpretation: A rising trend can increase cash pressure even when reported revenue is stable.
caveats: Receivables can reflect timing and accounting practices; interpret with payer mix and revenue cycle context.

label: Debt to assets
definition: Total liabilities as a share of total assets.
strategic_use: Used to assess leverage, solvency, and balance-sheet risk.
high_value_interpretation: A higher value may indicate greater leverage and less financial flexibility.
low_value_interpretation: A lower value may indicate less leverage or a stronger asset cushion.
trend_interpretation: A rising trend can indicate increasing balance-sheet risk, especially if margins are negative.
caveats: Facility balance sheets can be affected by ownership structure and related-party arrangements.
